source.label: thm:alpha_larger_than_0
source.quote: Let $\alpha >0$, the number of arms be $k = 2$ and $m^*_1>m^*_2$. Let $\Pi_0$ be a prior where $\mathbb{P}_{\Pi_0}(M_2 > M_1 ) > 0$. For any error threshold $\epsilon > 0$, there is a deterministic mapping $f(\Pi)$ such that for all $t\geq 0$: Sampling from $Q_t= f(\Pi_t)$ chooses arm $2$ with a constant probability. $D_{\alpha} (\Pi_t,Q_t) < \epsilon$. Therefore sampling from $Q_t$ for $T/10$ time-steps and using any policy for the remaining time-steps will cause linear frequentist regret.

results.notes: Existence of a bad approximation within epsilon alpha-divergence; not a lower bound for all algorithms. Constants depend on epsilon, alpha, Delta (see Lemma 5).

source.label: lem:regret1

results.notes: Per-round lower bound multiplied by T. Delta = m*_1 - m*_2. Bound for the specific constructed approximation.

source.label: thm:alpha_less_than_1_example
source.quote: Let $\alpha <1$, the number of arms be $k = 2$ and $m^*_1>m^*_2$. Let $\Pi_0$ be a prior where $M_2$ and $M_1 -M_2$ are independent. There is a deterministic mapping $f(\Pi)$ such that for all $t\geq 0$: Sampling from $Q_t=f(\Pi_t)$ chooses arm $2$ with probability $1$. For any $\epsilon >0$, there exists $ 0<z \leq 1$ such that if $\mathbb{P}_{\Pi_0}(M_2 > M_1)=z$ ... then $D_{\alpha} (\Pi_t, Q_t) < \epsilon$ ... Therefore sampling from $Q_t$ at all time-steps results in linear frequentist regret.

results.notes: Lemma 7 gives exact regret Delta*T for this construction (arm 2 chosen always).

source.label: thm:uniform_sublinear_regret
source.quote: Consider the case when Assumption~\ref{assumption:prior} or \ref{assumption:prior2} is satisfied. Let $\alpha \leq 0$ and $p_t= o(1)$ be such that $\sum_{t=1}^\infty p_t = \infty$. For any number of arms $ k$, any prior $\Pi_0$ and any error threshold $\epsilon > 0$, the following algorithm has $o(T)$ frequentist regret: at every time-step $t$, with probability $1-p_t$, sample from an approximate posterior $Q_t$ such that $D_{\alpha} (\overline{\Pi}_t, \overline{Q}_t) < \epsilon$, with probability $p_t$, sample an arm uniformly at random.

results.notes: Result is o(T) (sublinear), encoded as limsup of Regret/T equal to 0; no rate given.

source.label: thm:uniform_sublinear_regret
source.quote: Since the Bayesian regret is the expectation of the frequentist regret over the prior, for any prior if the frequentist regret is sub-linear at all points the Bayesian regret will be sub-linear.

results.notes: Sublinear Bayesian regret, encoded as limit of regret/T = 0.
